# Fair Isaac (FICO) - a deep dive on management and the setup

As of 2026-10-19. Live price $771.19 (New York listing, US dollars), up about 15% from $667.58 a week ago, 59% below the 52-week high of $1,858.91 and 32% above the 52-week low of $586.05. Transcripts read: five earnings calls from 4 February 2025 to 29 July 2026 (fiscal Q1 2025 through fiscal Q3 2026).

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Across the five calls the story moved from "pricing power plus a software turnaround" to "predictive superiority defends a price that the regulator is now attacking".

- February 2025 (fiscal Q1 2025): a confident pricing story. Scores revenue rose 23%, mortgage-origination revenue rose 110% "from both pricing and volume increases", and mortgage originations were 34% of Scores revenue. Software was framed as a platform migration.
- November 2025 and January 2026: the calendar-2026 rate card (the mortgage score price taken from $4.95 to about $10 per pull, per the prior record of this committee) arrives, together with the direct-licence programme, which lets lenders buy the score from Fair Isaac rather than through the three credit bureaus and introduces a per-closed-loan "performance" fee.
- April 2026: the company cut the upfront price of its newer Score 10T to $0.99, matching the rival VantageScore 4.0 headline price, and told the market it did not anticipate share loss in any vertical.
- July 2026 (fiscal Q3): the emphasis shifted to evidence of quality. Management led with the Milliman study on Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac data showing Score 10T beats VantageScore 4.0 on all three predictive measures in every origination year, with a more-than-10% advantage on first-time buyers. The 10T adopter programme reached 70 lenders (about 55% of top-50 originator volume). UltraFICO, built with Plaid cash-flow data, reached general availability. The direct-licence programme was still "under review by the GSEs" - the third consecutive quarter it was described as close.

The driver that was introduced and then quietly lost its footing: regulatory exclusivity. The mortgage price increases depended on Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac accepting only Classic FICO. That condition was withdrawn after the last call (4 September 2026 broad VantageScore acceptance; 9 September removal of approval requirement; 29 September single loan-level pricing grid treating Classic FICO and VantageScore 4.0 alike, effective for loans from 1 October 2026).

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | Financial evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Another strong quarter" (July 2026) | Q3 revenue $674M, up 26%; GAAP EPS $10.45, up 41%; trailing free cash flow $961M, up 28% (latest data feed shows $996M trailing to 30 June 2026) | Matches |
| Scores growth is durable | Scores +41% in Q3, but mortgage-origination revenue grew 97% on low-single-digit volume growth - almost entirely the price increase | Richer than the trajectory justifies: it is a one-time repricing, not volume |
| Software is a growth business | Software segment +2%; platform revenue +66%, non-platform -25% | Partly true: a fast platform half netted against a deliberately shrinking legacy half |
| Capital returned efficiently | $1.96B spent in Q3 alone on 1.705M shares at an average $1,149; stock now $771 | Poor timing: the company bought heavily about 33% above today's price and then paused buybacks to pay down debt |
| Balance sheet comfortable | Net debt $5.35B at 30 June 2026 (borrowings $5.58B plus $16M leases less $248M cash); negative shareholders' equity (return on equity reads -110%) | Leverage is the highest in the data-analytics peer group |
| Five-year compounding | Revenue $1.32B (2021) to $1.99B (2025); EPS $13.40 to $26.54; five-year EPS growth about 18.6% a year | Corroborated - the historic record is genuinely excellent |

Valuation models in our own screener disagree sharply: one owner-earnings model reads $1,936, while discounted cash flow, earnings power value and owner earnings read deeply negative and a 15%-return intrinsic value reads 21% below the price. The single bullish model capitalises a trailing cash flow built on the exclusive mortgage price.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Declining, from offensive to defensive.

- February 2025: offensive - growth from "pricing and volume", record buybacks.
- April 2026: still offensive - no share loss anticipated in any vertical.
- July 2026: defensive - the call opens with third-party validation of predictive power rather than with pricing, a sign the pricing argument now needs a defence. Per this committee's prior reading of the same call, the chief executive conceded volume loss is "not that easy" to detect and said "everything is on the table" on 2027 pricing.
- Since the call (October 2026): a roughly 15% workforce reduction framed as AI-driven restructuring (about $27M of severance in fiscal Q4), several shareholder-litigation investigation notices (29 September to 7 October), and one customer reaffirmation (United Wholesale Mortgage, 6 October).

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Medium. On reported numbers the company is reliable: it beat earnings in six of the last seven quarters and raised fiscal 2026 guidance in July 2026 (per the prior record: $2.53B revenue, adjusted EPS $42.43). On forward-looking competitive claims it is not: the April 2026 "no share loss anticipated" statement was overtaken by regulatory action within five months, and the direct-licence programme has slipped three quarters running. The beat record reflects a contractually locked annual price, which makes in-year guidance easy to beat and says little about the 2027 reset.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- The calendar-2027 mortgage rate card: asked repeatedly, never answered. It is normally published in the autumn and is still not public as of 19 October 2026.
- Whether lenders pull fewer FICO scores now that VantageScore 4.0 is accepted and priced at $0.99 (TransUnion, locked through 2028) or $4.50 (Equifax): management argues score shopping forces both pulls but cannot verify it.
- Timing of the direct-licence approval: repeatedly "waiting for their okay".
- Buybacks versus debt paydown: management chose debt.

Analysts have since cut targets (latest month average $1,096 versus $1,360 a year ago; Barclays $875 and Bank of America $700 at the low end), confirming the pressure points became bad news.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

Red flags
- 🔴 Fiscal Q3 2026: about 42% of revenue (mortgage originations at 62% of a Scores segment that is 68% of the company) rests on one price in one regulated channel.
- 🔴 September 2026: the regulator ended exclusivity and equalised pricing grids; the bureaus that distribute FICO own and discount the rival.
- 🔴 Fiscal Q3 2026: $1.96B of buybacks at about $1,149 a share funded partly by a new term loan; leverage now constrains capital returns.
- 🔴 Insiders: zero open-market purchases against five sales (3,792 shares) through the collapse.
- 🔴 October 2026: workforce cut of about 15% and multiple securities-litigation notices.

Green flags
- 🟢 July 2026: Milliman, using the enterprises' own data, found Score 10T more predictive in every year tested.
- 🟢 Cash generation remains elite: about $1B of trailing free cash flow, capital spending about 0.2% of revenue, Piotroski 8 of 9.
- 🟢 Platform software growing over 60% with very high revenue retention.
- 🟢 6 October 2026: United Wholesale Mortgage reaffirmed FICO on all broker pulls; Score 10T opens to Federal Housing Administration lenders on 1 January 2027.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- Vocabulary shifted from "pricing" to "predictiveness" and "value to the ecosystem" - a move from claiming price to justifying it.
- The April 2026 10T price cut to $0.99 conceded the rival's price point on the newer model while defending the older one at about $10 - an implicit admission that the headline price is contestable.
- Capital allocation flipped within one quarter from a record $1.96B buyback to "near-term cash goes to debt", and the 2026 restructuring now uses an AI-efficiency framing, a classic margin-defence pivot.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: turning. The company is shifting from a pricing-led growth engine to a defence of share and margin, with leverage and restructuring on the balance sheet.

The single most important thing to weigh before sizing: today's earnings are capitalising a mortgage price that no longer has regulatory protection. Until the calendar-2027 rate card and the fiscal Q4 2026 pull-volume data (early November 2026) are public, the cash flow that makes the stock look cheap cannot be trusted as a base.

Moat: an intangible-brand and regulatory-licence moat. Returns are still very high (return on invested capital about 41% to 59% depending on the measure, gross margin 82%) and still rising on reported numbers, but the reported rise is the price increase whose protection has just been removed. The regulatory-licence part of the moat is being dismantled; the predictive-quality part remains. Net: narrow and eroding, not wide.

Secular threat: material rather than terminal. The force is regulatory and distributor-driven score competition in mortgages, not AI or fintech displacement; FICO remains the standard in cards, auto and personal lending, and its predictive edge is independently verified. The cheapness is therefore partly a fear print and partly a genuinely smaller earnings base - which share is which will not be known until the 2027 price is published.

interrogator_dossier:
# FICO (Fair Isaac) - a deep dive on management and the setup
As of 2026-11-16 · live price $720.60 (NYSE, USD) · five earnings calls read (Q4 fiscal 2025, 2025-11-05, through Q4 fiscal 2026, 2026-11-04)

The short version: the reported numbers have never been better, and the business they describe has just been changed by a regulator. Fiscal 2026 (year to 2026-09-30) closed with revenue of $2.535B (+27%), GAAP earnings per share of $36.32 (+37%) and free cash flow of $1.034B (+40%). But on 2026-09-29 the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA, the regulator of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac) put the cheaper rival VantageScore 4.0 on the same mortgage pricing grid as the classic FICO score, and on 2026-11-04 management declined, for the first time in this run of calls, to give a fiscal 2027 forecast. The past four quarters are clean. The next four are the question.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

- **Q4 fiscal 2025 (2025-11-05):** the story is pricing power plus distribution control. Management launches the mortgage direct license program (resellers calculate and sell the FICO score themselves, cutting out the three credit bureaus), signs Xactus, and offers two price models: "a historical per score pricing model and a new performance pricing model". The tone on competition is dismissive: the bureaus "have provided free Vantage scores for years outside of mortgage, yet FICO has continued to successfully compete and win."
- **Q1 fiscal 2026 (2026-01-28):** guidance reiterated; buybacks continue at an average $1,707 a share; mortgage originations revenue +60% and 42% of Scores revenue. FICO Score 10T (the newer, more predictive model) is pitched as the next growth leg.
- **Q2 fiscal 2026 (2026-04-28):** guidance raised. Mortgage originations revenue +127% and 63% of Scores revenue: the Scores segment is now mostly a mortgage-price story. The first defensive note appears: on the regulator's score-modernization process, "I would not hold my breath," and an admission that "it's conceivable that Vantage could get some share."
- **Q3 fiscal 2026 (2026-07-29):** guidance raised again, and an accelerated share repurchase (a large buyback done at once and funded with a term loan) is announced. The predictive-advantage case leans on a Milliman study (10T beats Vantage 4 by more than 10% for first-time buyers). Management concedes the rival is "finally getting a little bit of traction in mortgage because of the Lender Choice program."
- **Q4 fiscal 2026 (2026-11-04):** after the FHFA decision, the narrative changes from charging more to keeping customers. A "FICO Preferred Program" holds the 2027 wholesale price flat for enrolled lenders, pricing becomes "bespoke" by customer, buybacks are paused to repay debt, and the company gives no fiscal 2027 guidance. Software (the decisioning platform, revenue +84%) is moved up front as the growth engine.

The thesis has contracted from "a toll road that reprices every year" to "a valuable score that must now win on predictiveness and price, plus a fast-growing software platform."

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim (quarter) | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Record year, revenue +27% (Q4 FY26) | Revenue $1.99B to $2.53B; Scores $1.652B (+41%), Software $883M (+7%) | Matches |
| Free cash flow growth (Q4 FY26) | $1.034B, +40%; trailing FCF margin about 42% | Matches |
| Growth is broad-based | Largely mortgage price: mortgage originations revenue +60% (Q1) and +127% (Q2), 42% then 63% of Scores | Narrower than the headline: one price lever drove most of the growth |
| Buybacks are "an attractive use of cash" (every call) | $3.028B repurchased in FY26 at an average $1,204, about 10% of shares; stock now $720, about 40% below that average | Capital destroyed on a large scale; partly debt-funded |
| Leverage is manageable, "a 1- or 2-quarter thing" (Q4 FY26) | Net debt $5.06B at 2026-09-30 (borrowings $5.26B plus $19M leases, minus $218M cash); 3.29x net debt to EBITDA | True today, but leverage sits on the very cash flow now under pricing pressure |
| Software is the growth engine (Q4 FY26) | Platform revenue +17%, +37%, +54%, +66%, +84% through the year; non-platform revenue -7% to -25% | Platform acceleration is real; the segment as a whole grew only 7% for the year |
| Quality of earnings | GAAP net margin 32.9%, Piotroski 8/9, Altman-Z 8.4; Q4 GAAP results include a $65M accrual for a proposed antitrust class-action settlement | Clean, with a real legal cost now booked |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY - Declining

- 2025-11-05: confident and offensive ("overwhelming interest" in the direct license program; guidance built with a "haircut" so it can be beaten).
- 2026-01-28 to 2026-07-29: still raising guidance, but each call spends more airtime defending predictiveness against Vantage.
- 2026-11-04: defensive. "We want to retain as much volume as we possibly can in the face of competition from Vantage"; on mortgage volume assumptions, "we're not going to start now"; on the post-election regulatory outlook, "your speculation is as good as ours." The shift from price increases to price holds and from buybacks to debt repayment is the clearest tone change in the record.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY - High on delivery, now absent

Fiscal 2025 guidance was beaten on every metric; fiscal 2026 guidance was reiterated (Q1), raised (Q2) and raised again (Q3), and the year delivered (EPS beat in 7 of 7 quarters in our scan). There is no sandbagging problem in the record. The issue is that the one forecast that matters, fiscal 2027 with the new mortgage pricing, has been withheld (2026-11-04). A management that historically guided conservatively choosing not to guide at all is itself information. Reliability: High on the past, untestable on the future.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Volume versus price in mortgage.** Asked directly (BofA, 2026-11-04) whether the goal is price or volume, the answer was "we try to optimize around both." No split was given.
- **Mortgage volume assumptions** (Wolfe, 2026-11-04): refused.
- **Vantage share gains through Lender Choice** (Q2 and Q3): answered with predictiveness studies, not with share data.
- **Regulatory direction after the 2026-11-03 elections:** no view offered.
- Analyst price targets have followed the stock down: last-year average $1,222, last-month average $866, newest targets $650 to $925 (2026-11-05/06).

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

Red flags
- The 2026-09-29 FHFA decision removed the classic FICO score's exclusive place in the conforming mortgage pricing grid. The stock fell about 26% that day.
- Fiscal 2027 guidance withheld (2026-11-04).
- $3.0B of buybacks at about $1,204 a share in FY26, partly funded by a term loan, left net debt at $5.06B just as the cash engine became contested.
- Concentration: mortgage originations were 42% to 63% of Scores revenue in the quarters disclosed, and Scores is about 65% of revenue and most of the profit.
- Insiders: 2 open-market buys (16 shares) against 34 sells (22,576 shares).
- A 15% workforce cut (2026-10-06) and a $65M antitrust settlement accrual (Q4 FY26).

Green flags
- The FHA will make FICO Score 10T available to approved lenders from 2027-01-01 (announced in Q4 FY26).
- Large lenders publicly enrolling in the Preferred Program: UWM (2026-10-06), Fairway, Movement, Rate (2026-10-30), Guild, New American Funding, PennyMac (2026-11-02), DHI, loanDepot, PRMG, CMG (2026-11-04).
- Direct license agreements with resellers covering about 73% of mortgage reseller volume.
- Software platform revenue +84% in Q4 FY26; analyst-firm leadership rankings (Gartner, Forrester, IDC).
- Free cash flow of $1.03B and gross margin of 86% give room to cut debt quickly.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The pricing vocabulary moved from "per score" and "performance model" (late 2025) to "bespoke," "tailored" and "no 2027 wholesale mortgage price increase" (late 2026). That is the language of a company defending share, not setting price.
- Management now stresses its "dedicated score sales force" and direct customer relationships: a hedge against the bureaus, which own VantageScore and are now open competitors rather than distribution partners.
- Nikhil Behl (president, Software) speaks more on the latest call, a sign that the software story is being moved forward to carry the investment case.
- The $10 Preferred Program bundle includes 10T at no extra charge. FICO is using its newer model to defend the price of the old one.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: turning. The reported numbers are still strengthening, but the business model is shifting from yearly mortgage price increases to defending volume at a flat or lower price, and from buybacks to paying down debt.

The single most important thing to weigh before sizing: **what the mortgage score earns after the reset.** Mortgage originations make up roughly half of Scores revenue at about 90% incremental margin, and the company carries $5.06B of net debt. A 25% fall in mortgage score revenue takes roughly $9 a share off after-tax earnings. A 50% fall, combined with that leverage, roughly halves the equity value. The first clean read is the Q1 fiscal 2027 report (expected around 2027-01-29), the first quarter under the new pricing and with 10T available through the FHA.

Moat: the score is a regulatory-license and switching-cost moat, with three decades of lender models, investor pricing and mortgage-bond analytics built on it. Returns have been rising (return on invested capital 47%, gross margin 86% and expanding), but the dated regulatory change has narrowed the moat in its most profitable use. The FHFA decision did not destroy the franchise: lenders are still choosing FICO, and it stays dominant in cards, auto and personal loans, where Vantage has been free for years. It did end FICO's pricing authority in conforming mortgage. Width: narrow and eroding in mortgage, still wide outside it. The threat is regulatory and competitive, not a technology that makes credit scoring obsolete. It is material, not terminal. The cheapness is partly fear, but mostly a real, measurable cut to the highest-margin revenue line. It is not a clean mispricing.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory turning · a narrow but real moat · moat trend eroding · structural threat material.
thesis_evidence: The value thesis rests on one load-bearing claim: that the mortgage score keeps most of its revenue after losing its exclusive place in conforming mortgage pricing. That claim is in doubt but not disproven. Against it: the FHFA put VantageScore 4.0 on the same pricing grid on 2026-09-29; FICO held its price instead of raising it (2026-10-23) and withheld fiscal 2027 guidance, citing pricing and volume uncertainty (2026-11-04). For it: Q4 fiscal 2026 (reported 2026-11-04) still showed Scores revenue of $414M, up 33%, and B2B scores up 39%; large lenders including UWM (2026-10-06), PennyMac and Guild (2026-11-02), and loanDepot and DHI (2026-11-04) publicly committed to keep pulling FICO scores; and the FHA accepts FICO Score 10T from 2027-01-01. The first quarter priced under the new regime settles it.
